messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: plans to put GMO in RStanArm, RStan, and Stan C++?
parts:
[moved from Dustin's personal repo to public stan-dev group]

see below.

> On Mar 1, 2016, at 3:39 PM, bgoodri <notifi...@github.com> wrote:
>
> On Tue, Mar 1, 2016 at 3:34 PM, Bob Carpenter <notifi...@github.com>
> wrote:
>
> > Is the idea to bypass Stan C++ and RStan and write GMO
> > directly into RStanArm?
> >
>
> No, Dustin / Andrew is planning for gmo() / gmo_lmer() / gmo_glmer() to be
> separate from rstanarm, but I am planning to have gmo be one of the
> algorithms available for users to choose for rstanarm. But I still think
> the algorithm should be part of Stan or failing that rstan. It is not
> really different from optimizing() or vb() from the UI perspective.

I agree that it should be coded in Stan in C++. I thought you
guys were all still working on the design --- at least Andrew tells
me it's premature for me to worry about this as it's just experimental.

So if that's still the case and all this discussion isn't about something
we're going to release any time soon, I'll go back to my regularly scheduled
day.

> > Can't you just take the fixed values and pass them into
> > log_prob as parameters and then ignore the resulting
> > gradients? It won't be as efficient as doing this all
> > the right way, but it should work and it probably won't be
> > any less efficient than what you're doing now by reconsituting
> > an entire model's data + fixed parameters.
> >
>
> Maybe.

If someone can lay out the API calls required from the model, we
can talk about updating the generated code to make it more
efficient. It seems unlikely we're going to want to manage two
separately compiled Stan models in a Stan C++ implementation.

- Bob

messages.author: 49e107cb0f8a3d27
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] plans to put GMO in RStanArm, RStan, and Stan C++?
parts:
It’s premature for you to worry about this as it’s just experimental. The code has mostly converged to a stationary point, but there are likely some changes to be made so there’s no need to think about its implementation in Stan’s C++ just yet. I think Ben would like to interface with the GMO R package once it’s released publicly, before it’s implemented in Stan’s C++.

Dustin

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] plans to put GMO in RStanArm, RStan, and Stan C++?
parts:
I'm curious, what are the reasons for keeping gmo_(g)lmer entirely separate from stan_(g)lmer? For the version of GMO where the user passes in their own Stan program(s) we won't have an equivalent in rstanarm, but for the lmer and glmer style models I think having both gmo_(g)lmer and GMO support for stan_(g)lmer will be confusing for users and add unnecessary work in that both sets of functions would need to be maintained (including providing support for users).

Jonah
